proposals.name: Cooling merger ejecta shell
proposals.idea: A stellar-merger luminous red nova ejected a shell that expanded to a roughly constant optical plateau. The shell is now cooling and forming dust, shifting its emission redward so the Wien-side g flux collapses faster than the r flux.

t_rise.meaning: photospheric expansion rise timescale in days

t_cool.meaning: time when cooling and reddening begin

A_b.meaning: plateau flux of band b in microjansky

s_b.meaning: post-cooling exponential fading rate of band b per day, larger in g than r

proposals.predicts: Unlike the flat blue TDE plateau, g will keep fading exponentially faster than r with continuing reddening, and r will subsequently fade toward zero without a blue recovery or second plateau.

proposals.name: Cooling SN plateau exit
proposals.idea: This is a hydrogen-rich core-collapse supernova, not a TDE: expanding ejecta rose slowly, stayed near recombination-plateau brightness, then began cooling and fading after about day -10. As the photosphere cools and recedes, blue light is suppressed much faster than red light.

equation.flux: amp_b * step(dt) * rise * cool * (tail_frac + (1 - tail_frac) * exp(-max(dt - t_plateau, 0.0) / tau_b))

t_plateau.meaning: plateau duration after explosion in days

tail_frac.meaning: fractional flux remaining on radioactive tail

amp_b.meaning: plateau flux per band in microjansky

tau_b.meaning: post-plateau decay time per band in days, shorter in g than r

proposals.predicts: After the plateau ends the g band will keep fading substantially faster than r, producing continued reddening and a transition to a slower faint tail, unlike the nearly flat blue plateau predicted by the TDE hypothesis.

proposals.name: Cooling plateau supernova cobalt tail
proposals.idea: This is a hydrogen-rich core-collapse supernova, not a blue persistent TDE: expanding ejecta produce the ~20 day rise and flat recombination plateau, after which the photosphere recedes and cools so the flux falls faster in g than in r. At late times the ejecta become powered mainly by radioactive cobalt decay, so the steep post-plateau fall must flatten.

equation.flux: step(dt) * A_b * rise * ((1 - f_tail) * exp(-decl / tau_cool_b) + f_tail * exp(-decl / tau_tail))

t0.meaning: explosion time in days relative to now

tau_rise.meaning: photospheric expansion rise timescale in days

t_break.meaning: end of recombination plateau and start of cooling decline

w_smooth.meaning: smoothness in days of plateau to decline transition

A_b.meaning: plateau flux per band in microjansky

tau_cool_b.meaning: post-plateau cooling decay time per band in days, shorter in g than r

f_tail.meaning: fraction of plateau flux entering the slow radioactive tail

tau_tail.meaning: radioactive cobalt tail decay time in days

proposals.predicts: The g band will keep fading faster than r so the source reddens, but both bands will flatten onto a ~90 day cobalt tail instead of remaining constant and blue as the TDE and null forecasts predicted.
